Describes Australia Awards among Australian Government scholarships

summary: Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term awards from the Australian Government (Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade) for citizens of developing countries, mostly in the Indo-Pacific, Africa and South Asia. Winners study a vocational, bachelor's, master's or doctoral course at an Australian institution and must then leave Australia for at least two years. Which countries, levels, fields and documents apply is set separately in each country profile. The award covers tuition, airfares, a one-time establishment allowance, a regular living contribution, health cover and an introductory academic programme, as listed under benefits.
eligibility_notes:
General rules (policy handbook, November 2025). You must be at least 18 years old on 1 February of the year the scholarship starts, be a citizen of a participating country, and live in and apply from an eligible developing country. A few exceptions to applying from your home country can be made, for example for people working for their government or a regional organisation in a third country. You may not be an Australian citizen or permanent resident, or be applying to live in Australia permanently. You may not be married, engaged or in a de facto relationship with an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident during application, selection and mobilisation. You may not be serving military personnel, may not have a criminal conviction (including child protection and sexual exploitation offences), and may not have received a long-term Australia Award in the previous four years.

You must also meet any extra condition set by your country programme (for example years of work in a sector), meet the admission rules of the Australian institution, and be able to get an Australian student visa. You cannot apply for a level lower than one you already hold, and awards are not given for courses you have already completed in Australia or that are available at universities in your home country at undergraduate level. You must tell the programme about any relationship with staff of the programme or its contractors. Intending migrants and people who give false information are excluded; fake documents mean automatic disqualification and a ban on future applications.

English: the policy minimum for awardees is IELTS Academic 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 84 with at least 21 in every part, or PTE Academic 58 with no skill below 50. Applicants whose first language is English and who were educated in English are exempt from the test. Scores are usually valid for two years and must be valid on 1 January of the start year. If the university asks for more, you must meet the university's score. Country programmes can lower the entry score for some groups and then provide English training before the award is confirmed (see the country snapshot).

Country rules differ a lot, so read your own profile. Snapshot of the 2027 profiles I read: Africa (25 countries) - Master's only, citizen of one of the 25 listed countries and living there, at least 25 years old on 1 February 2027, at least five years of postgraduate work in a field related to the study, in work when applying, a bachelor's degree, no Master's held or in progress, IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent. Bangladesh - Master's only, current employee in one of four target groups (civil service and bank or judicial cadres; NGOs and civil society; private sector; research, universities, media and culture), IELTS 6.5 or equivalent (6.0 with no band below 5.5 for people with disability, Indigenous people and marginalised gender groups), preference for five years of relevant work. Bhutan - Master's only, a four-year bachelor's degree plus three years of relevant full-time work (or the three-year-degree route), employer nomination letter, IELTS 6.5 or equivalent. Cambodia - Master's or PhD, live in Cambodia for the 24 months before the closing date, 24 months of paid work, no dual citizenship, IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5.5) for coursework Master's and 6.5 (no band below 6.0) for research Master's and PhD. Fiji - citizen living in Fiji, undergraduate or postgraduate, PhD not offered for 2027, three years of work in a priority sector for postgraduate study, course must not be offered by a local institution. Laos - citizen aged 18 to 50 on 31 December 2026, one year of residence in Laos, VET diploma, Master's (bachelor's plus two years of work) or PhD (Master's plus three years of work and IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0); general business and education management courses are excluded. Mongolia - Master's only, bachelor's GPA of at least 3.0, two years of continuous employment (not needed for verified disability), IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5. Nepal - Master's only, a bachelor's degree plus three years of relevant full-time work after it, IELTS 6.5 (6.0 with no band below 5.5 for women, people with disability, marginalised groups and public servants). Pakistan - Master's only, citizen living in Pakistan, 16 years of education, five years of relevant work, not more than 45 years old, development impact plan. Palau - citizen living in Palau; graduate certificate or diploma, bachelor's or Master's; TOEFL iBT 84 or equivalent. Papua New Guinea - citizen who works and lives in PNG, two years of work in the sector (not needed for people with disability), bachelor's only for courses not available in PNG. Timor-Leste - at least 18, 15 years of residence since 1999, no citizenship of a developed country, level-specific English and GPA rules. Vanuatu - at least 18 on 1 February 2027, citizen living in Vanuatu. Vietnam - Master's only, a university degree, 24 months of full-time relevant work, no second Master's, English and GPA rules by employer group.
age_experience_notes: Policy minimum age: 18 on 1 February of the start year. Country rules seen in 2027 profiles: Africa at least 25 on 1 February 2027 plus five years of postgraduate work; Laos aged 18 to 50 on 31 December 2026; Pakistan not more than 45 when applying and five years of relevant work; Timor-Leste at least 18 by the closing date; Vanuatu at least 18 on 1 February 2027. Work experience: Bhutan three years; Nepal three years after the bachelor's; Cambodia 24 months; Vietnam 24 months (12 months for people with disability or disadvantaged rural applicants); Mongolia two years of continuous employment; Palau two years for Master's; Laos two years for Master's (and for diploma applicants who already hold a diploma or degree) and three years for PhD; Fiji three years in the priority sector for postgraduate study; Solomon Islands three years related to the course for postgraduate study; Tonga three years for Master's and PhD; Timor-Leste nine months for bachelor's and two years for Master's; Papua New Guinea two years in the sector.
funding_summary: The scholarship is offered for the minimum time needed to finish the approved course, including any preparatory training. Maximum study time under the policy is four years for a bachelor's degree, two years for a Master's degree and four years for a doctorate; preparation programmes (English, foundation, qualifying) can add up to 12 months but the whole award may not run more than 12 months longer than the main course. Components: tuition fees; single economy airfare to Australia and home; visa costs; one-time establishment allowance of A$5,000; living contribution of A$99.26 a day from 1 January 2026 (about A$36,230 a year), paid fortnightly; compulsory four-to-six-week introductory academic programme; single Overseas Student Health Cover; supplementary academic support of A$500 every six months; fieldwork travel for research study; and, for some awardees, reunion airfare and disability support. Dependants are not funded.
programmes_note: There is no single course list. A course must be listed on the CRICOS register of courses for international students, fall in a priority area set for your country, and be at a level your country offers. Each country profile lists its priority fields; some exclude fields (for example general business or MBA-type degrees in Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam; no arts, business, computer science, law, nursing and some other degrees at bachelor's level in PNG). You give two course preferences in your application and cannot change them once you submit. At least two-thirds of the course must be taught in person; courses by distance and a few fields (nuclear technology, flying aircraft, military training) are not funded. An offer from a university is not needed when you apply.
institutions_note: Any Australian institution that offers your chosen CRICOS-registered course to international students, including universities, TAFE and vocational providers. After selection the country programme asks your first-preference institution for a place, and then the second if the first declines. The institution assesses you on merit and your English score, and can add a preparation programme. Some Pacific programmes also fund study in the Pacific, but those awards are a separate scheme not covered here.

summary.detail: Only some country programmes offer bachelor's awards (in the profiles I read: Palau, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste, Fiji, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands). Policy maximum is four years; double bachelor's degrees are allowed if both are in the original offer and fit within four years. A foundation or preparation programme of up to 12 months can be added. Not offered in Africa, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Mongolia, Nepal, Pakistan, Laos or Vietnam in 2027. Bachelor's study is not funded where the same course is available at universities in your home country.
summary.source_text: 2.6 Types of courses available to applicants

programmes.name: Fiji: undergraduate awards (Governance and Infrastructure only)
programmes.institution: Griffith University for aviation; other providers for infrastructure
programmes.detail: Bachelor of Aviation Management (Griffith University only); Construction Management; Marine/Maritime Engineering; Nautical Science; Naval Architecture. Entry: Fiji Year 12 or Year 13 aggregate of at least 320 out of 400 (English and best three subjects), or a mature applicant with a tertiary qualification and at least three years of relevant work. Minimum course length one year, maximum four.

programmes.name: Papua New Guinea: bachelor's degrees
programmes.detail: Only courses that cannot be studied in PNG, or for people with disability any course open to international students. Not available for arts, business, commerce, communications, computer science, cybersecurity, information technology, law, pilot training, management, nursing or public policy. Needs Year 12 completed and two years of work in the sector (not needed for people with disability).

programmes.name: Palau: Bachelor's degree and Bachelor of Aviation Management
programmes.detail: Palau Year 12 diploma, GED or adult high school certificate with a 3.5 cumulative GPA, no equivalent or higher qualification held. Aviation also has a professional-entry route (relevant degree, or five years in aviation with a professional or technical qualification).

programmes.name: Timor-Leste: Bachelor's / undergraduate degree
programmes.detail: About 15% of awards. IELTS 5.5 with no band below 5.5; senior high school GPA of at least 7.00 (or UNTL CBR Diploma 1 GPA of at least 2.50); at least nine months of professional or volunteer work. No priority fields, but the study must serve Timor-Leste's development priorities.

programmes.name: Vanuatu: Bachelor's degree
programmes.detail: English-language schooling: Year 13 grades A+, A or B in the top four subjects including English (or Year 12 grades of 1 or 2 if Year 13 is not finished); French-language schooling: grades of at least 12 out of 20 in all subjects including English. Priority areas include health, development studies, climate and renewable energy, inclusive education and STEM, IT, engineering and architecture, agriculture and others.

programmes.name: Solomon Islands: undergraduate awards
programmes.detail: Applicants may apply during or after Form 7 (Year 13); one year of related work is highly considered. Courses such as Bachelor of Teaching, Nursing and Medicine/Surgery are not sponsored. The embassy page is marked pending approval and mixes 2026 and 2027 years.

summary.detail: The most widely offered level, by coursework, by research, or a combination. Policy maximum is two years (the Master of Diplomacy double degree at the Australian National University may take three). Master's by research is meant for applicants who need high-level research skills and must name a suitable supervisor. Africa, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Mongolia, Nepal, Pakistan and Vietnam offer Master's only. A preparation or qualifying programme of up to 12 months can be added.
summary.source_text: 2.6.10 The maximum duration for a Master's degree program is two years

programmes.name: Africa (25 countries): Master's only
programmes.detail: Priority fields: agriculture and food security; climate change; foreign policy and international security; gender, disability and social inclusion; mining and energy. Eligible countries: Algeria, Angola, Botswana, Cote d'Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Tanzania, The Gambia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe.

programmes.name: Bangladesh: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: Priority areas include blue economy (fisheries and aquaculture, marine and maritime studies, seaports and shipping), health, sustainable development and environment (climate change, disaster management, water resources), social inclusion, inclusive economic development, public policy and governance, infrastructure, science and engineering (computer science, AI, cyber security, robotics) and security studies. Study period not more than two years.

programmes.name: Bhutan: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: Priority fields: accounting, finance and investment; actuarial science; agricultural technology and food science; business innovation; computer science (AI, machine learning); disability studies; education (curriculum, leadership, STEM); human resource management; law and legal studies; property valuation and asset management; applied statistics; structural engineering (bridge construction); tourism and hospitality management.

programmes.name: Cambodia: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: All fields welcome, climate-related and STEM study strongly encouraged. General management degrees including all MBA variants are not funded. Coursework: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5.5) or TOEFL iBT 60 or PTE 50; research: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0). About 1 to 2 years.

programmes.name: Fiji: postgraduate awards
programmes.institution: Griffith University for the aviation certificate
programmes.detail: Education (curriculum design, special and inclusive education, well-being and mental health, educational psychology); Environment (climate emergency, disaster risk, forestry, conservation and biodiversity, sustainable energy); Governance (Graduate Certificate in Aviation Management at Griffith, demography, international security); Health (digital health, speech pathology and audiology, rehabilitation counselling, occupational therapy); Infrastructure (construction management, geospatial science, maritime engineering). Maximum two years.

programmes.name: Laos: Master's degree
programmes.detail: Priority areas: economic development and trade; environment, climate and clean energy; agriculture and food security; gender, disability and social inclusion; governance and law; health and wellbeing; human resource development and education; infrastructure and connectivity. General business courses (such as business administration, accounting) and education management are excluded. Bachelor's degree and two years of work.

programmes.name: Mongolia: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: Wide range of fields; key areas include agriculture and environment, architecture and building, creative arts, education, engineering, food and hospitality, health, IT, management and commerce, natural and physical sciences, society and culture. Half of the awards go to the public sector and half to the private sector, civil society and international organisations.

programmes.name: Nepal: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: Priority areas: climate change; disaster risk reduction; economic development; education; gender equality, disability and social inclusion; governance; mental health and rehabilitation therapies; natural resource management; sustainable infrastructure development. The programme asks for recognition of prior learning, so you may be placed in a shorter programme.

programmes.name: Pakistan: Master's awards
programmes.detail: Priority areas: climate change; empowerment of women and girls; agriculture and water security; infrastructure; inclusive economic development. Recognition of prior learning will be requested.

programmes.name: Palau: Master's by research or coursework
programmes.detail: Priority areas: health; ICT; infrastructure development and management; fisheries management; electrical engineering; surveying and mapping or geodetic engineering; agriculture; education; law; tourism; aviation management (Griffith University); maritime studies. Needs a related first degree and two years of relevant work.

programmes.name: Papua New Guinea: Master's by coursework
programmes.detail: All areas available to international students in Australia. Not for people who already completed a Master's overseas; a PNG Master's holder may apply for a different field. Gender, climate and disability studies welcomed. Research Master's has a separate factsheet (not read).

programmes.name: Timor-Leste: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: No priority fields but the study must serve Timor-Leste development priorities (disability, health, workforce development, economic growth and diversification). IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5; recognised bachelor's degree with GPA of at least 2.75 and two years of relevant work.

programmes.name: Vanuatu: Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma and Master's
programmes.detail: Minimum university GPA of 3.0 (12 out of 20 for French-language study); a lower GPA can be considered with at least five years of highly relevant work.

programmes.name: Vietnam: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: Priority areas: agriculture, fisheries and forestry; digital transformation; IT (applicants with disability only); education; environment, climate change and energy; governance and economic growth; gender equality and disability; health; regional stability and human rights. Other fields except business administration considered on merit.

programmes.name: Philippines: Master's programmes
programmes.detail: The embassy notice announces Master's programmes starting in 2027 for leaders in the public service, private sector and civil society, with priority areas including agriculture, health, education, governance, climate change, energy and trade. Full profile not read.
programmes.source_text: Applications for the 2027 Australia Awards Scholarships are open for master's programs

programmes.name: Tonga, Solomon Islands: Master's by coursework or research
programmes.detail: Tonga: priority fields include governance and economics, health, infrastructure, sciences, environment and natural resources, education, and community development; three years of work for Master's and PhD. Solomon Islands: three years of work related to the course; priority fields include economic growth, governance, infrastructure, STEM, environment, education, health and community development.

summary.detail: PhD awards exist only in some country programmes (in the profiles I read: Cambodia, Laos, Timor-Leste, Solomon Islands; Indonesia's embassy notice names Master's or PhD). Policy maximum is four years. A PhD may need approval from the partner government, normally for people in or expected to take senior research or teaching posts. You must show in-principle support from a potential supervisor, and a research proposal is added after selection. If you go home before submitting the thesis you have at most two years to submit. Not offered in Africa, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Mongolia, Nepal, Pakistan or Vietnam, and not offered in Fiji for the 2027 intake.
summary.source_text: 2.6.17 The maximum duration for a PhD is four years

programmes.name: Cambodia: PhD
programmes.detail: Relevant completed Master's studies; IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0 (or TOEFL iBT 84 / PTE 58) obtained after 1 January 2025; two academic referee reports; evidence of extensive correspondence with the proposed supervisor.

programmes.name: Laos: Doctoral degree (PhD)
programmes.detail: Master's degree, at least three years of work, and IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0 taken after 30 March 2025 (IELTS fee reimbursed for eligible PhD applicants). Research proposal, two referee reports (one academic) and a supervisor's in-principle support letter are required.

programmes.name: Timor-Leste: PhD
programmes.detail: About 5% of awards, a limited number of research awards to strengthen Timorese academic and research institutions. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0; recognised Master's degree with GPA of at least 3.00.

programmes.name: Solomon Islands: PhD
programmes.detail: Listed as a level of study with three years of related work for postgraduate applicants; two academic referee reports, research proposal and a potential supervisor's written confirmation are required. Page is marked pending approval.

programmes.name: Tonga: Master's or PhD by research (documents)
programmes.detail: The document table refers to two academic referee reports for Master's or PhD by research. Three years of work in the chosen field for Master's and PhD.

programmes.name: Indonesia: Master's or PhD
programmes.detail: The embassy notice says postgraduate study (Master's or PhD) at an Australian university starting in 2027, assessed on professional skills and experience, personal attributes, academic competence and potential to lead. Full profile not read.

summary.detail: Vocational and diploma-level awards exist only in a few programmes. Policy lists vocational education and training courses among fundable course types. In the profiles I read: Laos (diploma and advanced diploma VET), Timor-Leste (diploma or advanced diploma, only for people with disability or people who lived outside Dili, Tibar and Metinaro in the last 12 months or more), Vanuatu (Certificate IV, diploma, advanced diploma, graduate certificate and graduate diploma) and Palau (graduate certificate or diploma).

programmes.name: Laos: Vocational Education and Training (diploma and advanced diploma)
programmes.detail: Upper secondary school completed or finishing by 30 September 2026; or under two years of tertiary study; or a diploma or bachelor's degree holder with two years of work seeking to fill a skills gap or change direction.

programmes.name: Timor-Leste: Diploma / Advanced Diploma
programmes.detail: IELTS 5.0 with no band below 4.5; senior high school GPA of at least 7.00 or UNTL CBR Diploma 1 GPA of at least 2.50; rural or municipal applicants must have graduated from a local high school.

programmes.name: Vanuatu: Certificate IV, Diploma and Advanced Diploma (TVET)
programmes.detail: All institution prerequisites, including strong English.
programmes.source_text: Certificate IV, diploma and advanced diploma

programmes.name: Palau: Graduate certificate / diploma
programmes.detail: Palau Year 12 diploma, GED or adult high school certificate with a 3.5 cumulative GPA.

benefits.limit_text: Academic fees: course costs and all compulsory international-student academic fees, paid direct to the institution
benefits.conditions: For the minimum period needed to finish the approved course, including preparation programmes. Maximum study time: bachelor's 4 years, Master's 2 years, doctorate 4 years; preparation up to 12 months. A student services amenities fee is also paid.

benefits.limit_text: Single economy airfare to Australia at the start and single economy airfare home at the end, by the most direct and economical route
benefits.conditions: Booked by the programme or institution. Reunion airfare is available only to unaccompanied awardees on awards of two years or more who meet the handbook rules. Fieldwork travel is funded for PhD and research Master's awardees and for coursework awardees with a compulsory fieldwork component.

benefits.limit_text: No separate housing payment. A once-only establishment allowance of A$5,000 on arrival helps with rental bonds, textbooks, study materials and extra insurance
benefits.conditions: The institution arranges moderately priced initial accommodation unless you decline in writing at least three weeks before arriving. Long-term housing is paid by you from the living contribution. No re-establishment allowance on transfer or after suspension.

benefits.limit_text: Contribution to living expenses: A$99.26 a day from 1 January 2026 (about A$36,230 a year), paid fortnightly
benefits.conditions: Starts on arrival (no earlier than 14 days before the introductory academic programme) and ends five days after the scholarship ends. Rate reviewed by DFAT. It is a contribution, not a full wage. Costs of family members are the awardee's own.

benefits.limit_text: Single Overseas Student Health Cover for the awardee for the whole stay
benefits.conditions: Does not cover pre-existing conditions or dental, physiotherapy and optical services; awardees pay those and any gap. Family cover for accompanying dependants is paid by the awardee.

benefits.limit_text: Compulsory Introductory Academic Programme of 4 to 6 weeks, paid direct to the institution
benefits.conditions: Failing to attend can mean losing the scholarship.

benefits.limit_text: Supplementary academic support of A$500 for every six months on award (A$1,000 a year)
benefits.conditions: Spent through the institution on tutoring, academic workshops, thesis editing, printing and binding and similar approved items; cannot be spent in advance.

benefits.limit_text: Student visa expenses (visa processing and medical checks) and preparation programmes (pre-course English, foundation or qualifying programmes)
benefits.conditions: Pre-course English in Australia only if you are within half an IELTS point (or 10 TOEFL iBT points or 7 PTE points) of the institution's score, for up to six months. Preparation programmes up to 12 months in total.

benefits.limit_text: Disability support (reasonable adjustments and accommodations), where assessed as needed
benefits.conditions: Medical treatment, medicines, prescription glasses and similar items are not funded.
The handbook says the Australian Government gives no financial support for family members who come with the awardee; awardees pay for their own health cover, accommodation and flights.

requirements.text: Certified copy of your original graduation certificate, with a certified translation if it is not in English (general list in the policy handbook; country profiles may replace or add to it).

Certified copies of original academic transcripts, with certified translations if not in English. Several profiles (Nepal, Cambodia, Laos, Bangladesh) ask for transcripts of all study, complete or incomplete.
Certified copy of a citizenship document such as a passport or national identity card. Use your full name exactly as in the passport, with no nicknames or abbreviations.
Certified copy of your birth certificate, with a certified translation if not in English.
requirements.conditional_rule: General handbook list; some country profiles accept other proof of identity

requirements.text: Curriculum vitae listing work history, responsibilities and research experience where relevant. Several countries require their own CV template and page limit (Laos: up to 6 pages; Fiji: up to 3 pages).

Referee reports: at least one academic and one other (for example a work supervisor), in the programme's template. Master's by research and PhD applicants provide two academic reports. Some countries ask for three (Nepal and Bangladesh for research Master's) or none for coursework (Cambodia).

English test certificate (IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT or PTE Academic) valid on 1 January of the start year. Not needed if your first language is English and you were educated in English. Some programmes do not require it at application (Fiji, Laos for non-PhD) or sponsor a test after shortlisting.
requirements.conditional_rule: Depends on country profile and your first language

requirements.text: PhD applicants: evidence (letter or email) that a potential supervisor supports your research topic in principle. If awarded, an additional research proposal is sent to the institution. Master's by research applicants in several countries (Nepal, Bangladesh, Laos, Solomon Islands) submit a proposal and supervisor support with the application.
requirements.conditional_rule: Doctoral and research Master's applicants only

requirements.text: Reintegration plan (also called development impact plan or re-entry action plan): a statement of realistic tasks where you will use your new skills after returning home, constraints and how you would handle them. Applicants must propose one as part of the application; many countries have a template.
requirements.conditional_rule: Required in the application under the handbook; template format set by country

requirements.text: Employer or government documents: employment letters or statements, employer nomination or endorsement letter, no-objection certificate or approval letter for public-sector applicants (for example Bhutan, Pakistan, Laos, Timor-Leste, Vanuatu, Bangladesh, Mongolia).
requirements.conditional_rule: Where the country profile requires it

requirements.text: Statement of good character or police check, which the programme uploads when it asks an Australian institution for a place; Palau asks for a police clearance with the application. A medical check is done for the student visa and paid by the programme.
requirements.conditional_rule: After selection, or at application where the profile says so

requirements.text: Certification rules: a copy must be sworn as a true copy by an authorised person (the institution's records office, an Australian overseas mission or a notary public) who writes a statement, signs, prints name, address and phone, gives their role and the date, and adds an official stamp. You may not certify your own documents or use a relative. A change of name needs proof such as a marriage certificate. Some programmes do not require certification at application (Laos, Cambodia, Africa) but ask for originals from successful candidates.
requirements.conditional_rule: Check your profile for when certification is needed

requirements.text: Upload rules: in the OASIS system each file is limited to 2 MB (Fiji brochure); several programmes ask you to combine documents into single colour PDFs by category, legible and in page order, and to use the current-year templates (an old template can make the application ineligible).

application_steps.title: Read your country profile and check you are eligible
application_steps.detail: Each participating country has its own profile that sets the opening and closing dates, levels, priority fields, extra eligibility rules, documents and how to apply. Check it against the general eligibility rules before starting. For the 2027 intake the profiles I read opened on 1 February 2026 and mostly closed on 30 April 2026 (Palau closed 30 June 2026); closing times differ by country.

application_steps.title: Choose a course and two preferences
application_steps.detail: Research courses on the CRICOS register for international students and give two course and institution preferences (ideally at two institutions, with their CRICOS codes). You do not need a university offer to apply, and an offer does not help your score. Preferences cannot be changed after you submit. Research applicants should find a suitable supervisor.

application_steps.title: Prepare documents, reintegration plan and referee reports
application_steps.detail: Gather certified documents, CV, referee reports, English test results, and your reintegration plan, using the templates your country programme publishes. Ask referees early, because they must file before the closing date. Declare all previous study and any relationship with programme staff; leaving out study can count as fraud.

application_steps.title: Submit the online application before the closing date
application_steps.detail: Most programmes take applications in the DFAT online system OASIS, using a personal email address. The system is slow near the closing date, so submit early; documents received after closing are not considered. Some countries add a route: Cambodia allows a hard-copy application at the embassy for people without internet, and the Philippines points to its own programme website. Fiji lets you un-submit and edit before the closing date. Incomplete applications are not assessed.

application_steps.title: Eligibility check and shortlisting
application_steps.detail: The country programme checks that you are eligible and your application is complete, then ranks eligible applications against the selection criteria; only shortlisted applicants are contacted. Laos runs an independent assessment, IELTS preparation and testing before interviews and applies a moderation step for gender, disability, province and ethnic background. Programmes encourage applications from women, people with disability and other marginalised groups.

application_steps.title: Interview and merit assessment
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed by a panel that includes the Australian Government and is chaired by a DFAT officer; group activities may be added (Bangladesh may also use a written test). All applications are judged on merit against professional and personal leadership qualities, academic competence and potential to contribute to development in the home country. The handbook gives a scoring guide from 'limited' (below 60%) to 'outstanding' (90% and above).

application_steps.title: Selection outcome and reserve list
application_steps.detail: Each country gets as many successful candidates as it has awards, usually plus ranked reserves who may be chosen if places free up. Applicants are told of the outcome when selection ends, generally in August under the handbook; the 2027 profiles gave August 2026 (Vietnam), August or September 2026 (Mongolia), September 2026 (Bangladesh and Laos) or late 2026 (most others). Success is provisional until you have a university place, the English score needed and a visa.

application_steps.title: Placement at an Australian institution
application_steps.detail: The programme asks your first-choice institution for a place through OASIS (by 25 August for first-semester starts and 15 March for second-semester starts), then your second choice if needed. The institution answers within 15 business days for coursework and 30 for research and may add preparation courses. If no placement is possible the offer is withdrawn. If your English is below the course score you may get pre-course English training (up to six months in home country or in Australia) and a preparation programme (up to 12 months in all).

application_steps.title: Sign the offer letter and contract
application_steps.detail: You receive a letter of offer and a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia. You become an awardee when you sign it. By signing you agree to the scholarship conditions: study full time and make satisfactory progress, start in the year awarded (an award cannot start after November; deferral only if DFAT agrees), do not hold another Australian Government scholarship, do not apply for any visa other than the student visa, and repay all benefits if you breach the conditions.

application_steps.title: Pre-departure briefing, visa and travel
application_steps.detail: You attend course counselling and a pre-departure briefing, and you must meet the Department of Home Affairs rules for a Student visa (subclass 500); the programme pays visa costs and books your flight. Travel depends on Australian government requirements. Dependants can only come if conditions are met and at your own cost.

application_steps.title: Arrive, complete the introductory programme and study
application_steps.detail: You arrive no earlier than 14 days before the compulsory introductory academic programme (4 to 6 weeks) and receive the A$5,000 establishment allowance. You then study full time, keep in touch with your institution's student contact officer, and report changes in your circumstances. You can lose the scholarship for poor progress, misconduct, fraud or breach of conditions; suspensions, extensions and transfers need approval.

application_steps.title: Return home and stay out for two years
application_steps.detail: When the award ends you must leave Australia and may not stay or apply to return for more than short visits for at least two years (time spent in Australia adds to the period). If you stay or get another visa you must repay the cost of the scholarship. Awardees are expected to book completion travel within 30 days of the end date, update their reintegration plan and join the alumni network. Research students who leave before submitting must submit the thesis within two years.
